about: Heredoc end markers as written after <<, and the line each shell ends the body at (claude-config#3566).
The one list of markers for both shell readers. lib/shell-words.py's heredoc_opener is held to it:
test-shell-words-heredoc.sh runs every row against the shells of its machine and then the reader.
mod-kit's readDelimiter (hooks/commands.ts) is not: its suite does not read this file, which is what
Each row was measured by running the text  cat <<WORD / v=$((1+1)) / LINE / echo RAN  (one piece
per line) in each shell, as a -c text, a file and an eval: the shell ends the body at LINE when
it prints a line RAN, and expands the body when it prints v=2. closes maps each LINE to the shells
that end the body there, by a group's name or a list of shells; never lists lines no shell ends
it at; a shell named under no LINE ends it at none of them. quoted says the body is not expanded.
The rows say what these seven shells did, not what any shell called bash or sh does: on Linux sh is
often dash and bash is newer. So shells gives each one's run command, a probe that prints what it
is, and prints, how the probe's output starts for the shell that was measured (dash has no version
to print, so its probe names the system). A suite holds a shell to the rows only where the probe
prints that, and says the rest is unmeasured.
A reader that vouches for its reading must give the LINE all seven shells share. Where they do
not share one it must say so (shell-words.py names the heredoc in unsure), and where bash and
zsh share one its marker must be that LINE.
measured: 2026-11-24 on macOS: bash 3.2.57 (as bash, as bash --posix and as sh), dash, zsh 5.9 (as zsh and emulating sh) and ksh 93u+
